topics.topic: Closed refusal-code vocabulary and assignment to semantic refusals
questions: What is the closed refusal-code vocabulary, and which semantic refusals decided in State 2 share a code or receive distinct codes before `REFUSAL_HTTP_STATUSES` can contain one row per code?
What is the closed set of refusal codes for which REFUSAL_HTTP_STATUSES must contain one row?
What is the closed refusal-code vocabulary for which `REFUSAL_HTTP_STATUSES` must contain exactly one row? The supplied texts name several codes but never give the exhaustive set.

quotes:
The codes are
distinct where a caller acts on the difference; the kinds are a closed set
the owner interface renders and State 6 declares as `models`' vocabulary.

| code | stage | kinds | who acts on it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `unauthenticated` | (1) | `no_valid_token` — missing, unknown or wrong, one answer (A17 rule 7); `no_owner_session` — none, ended or expired (A13 rule 2); `sign_in_refused` — wrong or missing credential or a lockout, one answer (A13 rule 4) | the service fixes its token; the owner signs in |
| `not_permitted` | (1) | `outside_service_rights` (A09 rule 3); `csrf_refused` (A13 rule 5); `answer_above_class` (A09 rule 4) | the caller is not allowed this call |
| `confirmation_refused` | (1) | `confirmation_not_pending` — the session holds no pending value: never shown, used up or cleared; `confirmation_other_value` — another value while the pending one is valid, which stays; `confirmation_bound_elsewhere` — the pending value given for another action, target, revision or inputs, now used up; `confirmation_expired` — cleared (A13 rule 6) | the owner submits the pending step again, or has it shown again |
| `not_found` | (2) for `agent_call_refused`, (3) for the others | `agent_call_refused` — an unregistered session, a project outside the set, none active, an unknown pointer for Kernel: one answer, always of stage (2) (A10 rule 3, A08 rule 7); `unknown_project`, `unknown_customer`, `unknown_room`, `unknown_pointer`, `unknown_session` (State 0) | the caller re-reads |
| `invalid_request` | (4) | `missing_value` (A02 rule 1); `malformed_request_id` (A01 rule 1); `outside_closed_list` (A19 rule 3) — a value outside its enumeration, an
object kind or a customer language included (A02 rule 4); `outside_form` — a
present value outside the form State 1 declares: an alias over the imported
`ALIAS_MAX_CHARACTERS` constant, a floor area not greater than the imported
`OBJECT_FLOOR_AREA_MIN_EXCLUSIVE`, a number of rooms that is not a whole
number of at least the imported `OBJECT_ROOMS_MIN`, a floor that is not a
whole number (A02 rule 4); `duplicate_pick` — a project, or a Customer's v1 value, given twice (A16 rule 1); `unknown_artifact_type` (A22 rule 5); `date_after_today` (A15 rule 3, R0-84); `file_too_large`; `file_unreadable` — bytes that do not parse as the format States 5 and 6 declare, or an upload whose body fails or ends before its declared length; `file_malformed` — a file that parses but holds two projects with one id, or a project whose id or status is missing or not of its field's shape; a status outside its vocabulary is not this, but a malformed record of a pick (A16 rule 4) (A19 rule 4, A16 rule 3) | the caller fixes the request |
| `stale` | (5) | `stale_revision` (A04 rules 2, 3); `stale_access_version` (A12 rule 3) | the owner reads again |
| `refused` | (6) | `archived`, `active` (erasing an active project), `anonymised`, `erased`, `customer_restricted`, `customer_ended`, `customer_erased`, `conflict` (A01 rule 5), `not_granted`, `not_pending`, `withdrawn`, `superseded`, `import_closed`, `file_not_kept`, `mapping_not_clean`, `no_picks` | the owner reads the record's state |
| `internal_error` | — | `transaction_failed`: a store transaction did not commit, nothing changed (A04 rule 4) | the caller reads again before repeating |
judgement.why: State 5 supplies the exhaustive refusal-code vocabulary and assigns every semantic refusal kind to a code.
options: Use distinct stable codes for semantic refusals.
Group semantic refusal kinds under the closed State 5 codes.
Preserve only v1 codes.
consequences: The later table fixes the public distinctions and makes `REFUSAL_HTTP_STATUSES` total over its code vocabulary.

topics.topic: Exhaustive owner-action routes, HTTP methods, paths, and path-parameter representation
questions: What exact path is assigned to each owner action, and how are path parameters represented?
What exact path is assigned to every owner action, and how are path parameters represented in OWNER_ACTIONS?
What is the exhaustive owner-action vocabulary, and what exact method and path does each row of `OWNER_ACTIONS` use?

quotes:
An owner
action is addressed by its row of the data provider's `OWNER_ACTIONS`
(row model `OwnerActionRoute`, one row per `OwnerAction` member): a read
by `GET`, every other action by `POST`, at the path `/` and the action's
value, the project list at `/`; the row also says whether the action is a
change, whose form carries the CSRF value (A13 rule 2), and whether it
touches an uploaded file (A16 rule 2) — `show_confirmation` touching one
only when its `confirm_action` is `confirm_import`. A method and path of
no row name no action: `OwnerRequest.action` is then none, and
`operations` refuses the request after stage (1) as `invalid_request`
(`outside_closed_list`) at stage (4). The target is the query parameter
`OWNER_TARGET_PARAMETER` (`target`) names, an identity and never a
personal value (R0-29).
judgement.why: State 6 fixes one route per `OwnerAction`, the method rule, path construction, project-list exception, and query-parameter representation of targets.
options: One route row per owner action with target identities in the `target` query parameter.
Separate page and submission rows.
Derive route families without concrete rows.
consequences: The later contract chooses the first structure, with the project list at `/` and other action paths formed from `/` and the action value.

topics.topic: Import-confirmation binding and unique upload-occurrence numbering
questions: Does an import confirmation bind the upload number as M21 requires, bind only "the file's digest and the picks" as A13 rule 6 says, or is every pending import confirmation cleared by any accepted replacement upload? State 2 must also say how the upload number changes so two accepted uploads in one session can never reuse it.
Is an import confirmation bound to the particular upload occurrence, including M21's upload number, or only to the uploaded bytes' digest and the other displayed inputs?
How is the upload occurrence represented and generated once State 2 explicitly requires it in confirmation binding?

Does an import confirmation bind the upload number as well as the file digest? A13 rule 6 and A16 rule 2 describe the binding as the file digest and picks, but M21 and A16 Required test 3 require a same-bytes re-upload to invalidate the earlier confirmation.
How is the distinct per-upload value produced and represented while preserving the rule that even another upload of the same bytes replaces the prior upload?

quotes:
The admitted session; the action; its target; the revision or access
version the step shows, or that it shows none; the action's inputs — for an
erasure its choice, for the import the upload's number and the file's
digest with the picks, names, aliases and Customer values, for an erasure
of old entries the date.

The upload's number in the session: 1 for the session's first accepted
upload, then one more than the session's last, so two uploads of the same
bytes are two uploads (A16 rule 2).

The import's
confirmation step carries, besides the picks, the bound upload's number
and digest as the fields `upload_number` and `file_digest` of
`OwnerValues`, rendered from the step's `ImportInputs`, so its submission
binds what was shown (owner, 2026-11-24).
judgement.why: The later texts bind import confirmation to both upload number and digest and define the upload number as a session-local integer beginning at 1 and increasing on every accepted upload.
options: Bind the upload number and digest and increment the number for every accepted upload.
Clear confirmations independently on replacement.
Bind only the digest and allow an identical re-upload to match.
consequences: The decided binding refuses an old confirmation after any accepted replacement upload, including one with identical bytes.

Every request is checked at its arrival, and only then — the reading of

topics.topic: Digest collision guarantees and canonical encoding of hashed input tuples
questions: What guarantee must a digest provide when it identifies an accepted import, distinguishes an uploaded file, or binds confirmation inputs: must distinct byte strings or input tuples always be treated as distinct, or is cryptographic collision resistance only an operational assumption? The texts also do not decide the canonical encoding of the ordered input tuple before hashing.

quotes:
An action that asks for confirmation (Identity formats) is submitted with a
   confirmation value Registry made when it showed the step: one-time, kept in
   the owner session, bound to the action, its target, the revision or access
   version the step showed, or that it showed none when the action has
   neither (a record without a revision, A04 rule 3, among them), and its
   inputs — for the import, the file's digest
   and the picks — kept as a digest of those values in a fixed order, never
   as the values themselves; a submission's inputs are bound when their digest
   equals it.

The owner confirms that mapping in the confirmation
   step (A13 rule 6); the confirmation applies the file of that digest, the
   picks, names, aliases and Customer values the mapping showed, nothing
   else; a file no longer kept is refused and must be uploaded again.

The file and the
   picks are bound by their digest, the names, aliases and Customer values
   with them, so the mapping it builds is the one the step showed but for
   the ids production gained in between;
judgement.divergence: With an ambiguous encoding or colliding digest, a submission carrying different picks or Customer values can compare equal and apply values the confirmation step did not show; with an injective encoding plus collision handling, the same submission is refused, which the owner observes as an accepted import versus a refusal.
judgement.why: State 2 requires the confirmation to apply only the mapping shown but leaves open whether digest equality can equate distinct input tuples and how the ordered tuple is encoded.
options: Specify a canonical encoding and collision-resistant digest, treating cryptographic collision as outside the guarantee.
Compare exact input values in addition to the digest so distinct tuples can never satisfy the binding through a collision.
Treat digest equality as identity without a collision or encoding guarantee.
consequences: The first option makes ambiguity impossible but treats cryptographic collisions as an operational assumption.
The second preserves the guarantee even under collisions but requires retaining or reconstructing exact bound values.
The third permits a different tuple to be applied under an encoding ambiguity or collision, breaking the stated mapping guarantee.

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
State 2: decide required results and constraints, including necessary refusal precedence; carry test mechanisms, exact contracts and deployment procedures to their owners.
